questions.enonce_markdown:
**SECTION A - DIRECTED WRITING (30 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content (14 marks); Expression and Accuracy (12 marks); Slanting (04 marks).

You are a social worker and you have observed that early girl child marriages are still rampant in your community. Write a talk to be delivered on radio, on the reasons for this practice and the consequences on the girl child. Write in such a way that will convince the public to desist from such practice. Write in TWO paragraphs of not more than **150 words**, paying attention to grammar, spelling, punctuation and handwriting.

**EARLY GIRL CHILD MARRIAGE**

It is common place in Cameroon to find young girls before the age of eighteen being propelled into early marriages. A parent of low socio-economic standing, having many children and in an overcrowded home, may send off one of the daughters prematurely into marriage as the only means of reducing the family load or amassing wealth for their livelihood. Some parents are of the notion that it is inherent in their religious beliefs and culture not only to get married to virgins but to marry as many as are capable. It is this urge to get married to virgins that pushes them to go for the unspoiled teenagers, which in most cases are aged between nine and thirteen.

In a bid to avoid shame and disgrace some parents force their teenage daughters with unwanted pregnancies into early marriages. Such parents consider this a better option than to allow their daughters to go in for an abortion. Some lazy young girls see early marriages as a way out of a long and tedious education or as a short cut to an easy and comfortable life, especially if married to a man of good socio-economic standing. No matter the reasons, the health consequences may be disastrous.

Any traumatic exercise such as difficult delivery may cause perinea tear or rupture of the uterus and surrounding structures. These may also cause faecal or urinary incontinence. Infections may ensue, resulting from poor treatment or from direct contamination by a chronically infected older or polygamous husband. Some of these chronic infections like gonorrhoea or genital TB can lead to infertility.

Female homones alter the chemical constitution of connective tissue making it more pliable, making the stretching of the cervix possible, making the relaxation of the joint capsules possible and making the pelvic joints mobile.

In some areas young girls are being betrothed to old men, who initially play the role of father and uncle to the girl but ultimately get married to the girl. Apparently, these young girls are traumatised and forced to play the role of house wives

Socially, premature marriages cause a disruption in the child's education or career and such a young mother may subsequently find herself in the same classroom or examination centre with her son or daughter. Also, most early marriages are not founded on love, and this may lead to early divorces and the resultant consequences for the whole family.

Early girl child marriage, like female genital mutilation should be completely discouraged and vehemently condemned in our society. Our civil and religious authorities have a moral role to play by rejecting such couples and refusing to legalise or bless such marriages.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model answer (two paragraphs, 143 words)**

Dear listeners, early girl child marriage is still rampant in our community, and we must stop it. Some poor parents with many children marry off their daughters to reduce the family load or gain wealth. Others believe a girl must marry as a virgin, so they push girls as young as nine into marriage. Some force pregnant teenagers to marry to avoid shame. Some girls even see marriage as a shortcut to an easy life.

These reasons can never justify the consequences. Childbirth may tear a young girl's womb and cause incontinence, while infections can lead to infertility. Many girls are traumatised when given to old men. Their education is destroyed, and loveless unions often end in divorce. Dear listeners, let us keep our daughters in school, and let civil and religious leaders refuse to bless such marriages. Our girls deserve a future.

**Why this works (selection and slanting).** The talk must give the REASONS for early marriage and the CONSEQUENCES on the girl, and it must convince listeners to stop. Paragraph one keeps the reasons from the passage (poverty and a large family, the wish to marry virgins, shame over pregnancy, the idea of an easy life). Paragraph two keeps the consequences (birth injuries and incontinence, infections and infertility, trauma, lost education, divorce) and ends with a direct appeal. The passage points that only describe medical processes (for example the effect of female hormones on connective tissue) or that repeat the same idea are left out. The tone is firm and persuasive (greeting, "we must stop it", call to action), every sentence is rephrased in the candidate's own words, and the text is in TWO paragraphs under 150 words, as the question demands.

**Marking guide**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content | 14 | Relevant reasons AND consequences taken from the passage (about 8 well-chosen points), with no unrelated material |
| Expression and Accuracy | 12 | Own words (no lifting of whole sentences), varied linking, correct grammar, spelling and punctuation, TWO paragraphs, 150 words at most |
| Slanting | 4 | The whole talk is aimed at convincing the public to desist: a persuasive tone, rhetorical appeal and a call to action |

**Common mistakes**

1. Copying whole sentences from the passage: the instructions say indiscriminate copying earns no marks.
2. Giving only the reasons or only the consequences, or writing a summary instead of a persuasive radio talk.
3. Writing one paragraph or three or more instead of TWO, or going over 150 words.

incertitudes: Le passage porte les fautes d'impression du sujet (par exemple « perinea », « homones », « house wives » sans point final, « common place »), recopiees telles quelles.
Le sujet demande DEUX paragraphes (la session 2023 en demandait un seul) : le modele est ecrit en deux paragraphes.
